topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the cancer lecture series, and the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Cancer causation, intrinsic mutations, and environmental risk factors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the foundational concepts of cancer etiology, weighing the contributions of intrinsic genetic mutation and bad luck against environmental and lifestyle exposures supported by epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer and Burkitt lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents drive oncogenesis, focusing in depth on the viral and environmental mechanisms underlying Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how physical and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation in the body to cause DNA adducts, mutations, and oxidative damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, non-mutagenic mechanisms, and physiological susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the concepts of tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and developmental susceptibility windows in carcinogenesis, concluding with a summary of these mechanistic pathways.

topics.label: Methods for detecting carcinogens and assessing cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the experimental, genomic, and epidemiological methodologies used to prove carcinogenicity, as well as the practical assessment of carcinogen risks versus benefits.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a final take-home summary and closes the lecture.
